description:

As a Transmission Planning Engineer Intern you will be working in the Transmission Planning group to develop and test solutions that improve future transmission system reliability and capacity. You will gain exposure to analysis, modeling and operations and see how planning studies, system models, and operations coordination work together within the MISO and PJM markets.

As a Transmission Planning intern you will:

- Support steady-state power-flow and short-circuit studies using industry tools such as PSS®E, TARA, and DSA Tools

- Assist with transmission interconnection and reactive-compensation studies for new large load and generation

- Help build and maintain the steady-state, dynamics, and short-circuit representations of the AES transmission system, keeping base cases current with topology, equipment, and rating changes

- Support NERC modeling data processes — MOD-032 data collection, FAC-008 facility ratings — and model validation against actual system performance

- Gain exposure to transmission operations planning, outage coordination, and RTO submission systems (MISO CROW, PJM eDART)

- Learn how AES works within the MISO and PJM markets and the NERC/FERC regulatory framework

- Attend site visits to substations and other facilities to see transmission infrastructure firsthand and learn how complex systems are built and operated

- Work in an agile, collaborative environment, partnering with engineers, technicians, and regulatory experts to solve complex problems

- Participate in formalized AES-specific learning opportunities to further your knowledge toward accelerating the responsible energy transition

- Network with peers, AES leaders, and like-minded employees through dedicated events, lunch-and-learns, and speaker series

- Actively engage in open discussions to help identify ways AES can better prepare for the future of energy

Requirements:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related field

- Coursework in power systems, circuits, or electric machines

- Problem-solving mindset and willingness to learn

- Ability to communicate clearly, verbally and in writing

Highly Desired:

- Exposure to power-flow or short-circuit software (PSS®E, TARA, ASPEN, CAPE, DSA Tools, or similar)

- Familiarity with the NERC/FERC/PJM/MISO regulatory landscape

- Coursework or project experience in power system analysis

description:

If you're ready to be part of a company that's not just adapting to change, but driving it, AES is the place for you. We're not just building a more sustainable future ,  we're powering it. Apply now and energize your career with a true leader in global energy.

AES Indiana is looking for a NERC Compliance Engineer to help strengthen the reliability, safety, and performance of our power generation operations. In this role, you will support renewable and thermal generation assets by helping ensure compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) and Regional Entity standards, while partnering closely with engineering, operations, and regulatory teams.
This is an opportunity to apply your technical expertise in a collaborative environment where your work directly supports reliable energy service and contributes to the global energy transition.

What You’ll Do

- Monitor, interpret, and support implementation of applicable NERC Reliability Standards for generation facilities.

- Develop, maintain, and execute compliance programs, procedures, and documentation in partnership with the NERC Compliance team.

- Support coordination of NERC and Regional Entity audits , spot checks, and self-certifications.

- Analyze protection system settings, generator performance models, and operational data to ensure compliance.

- Collaborate with plant engineers and operators to integrate compliance requirements into design changes, maintenance, and operational practices.

- Maintain accurate compliance records, evidence, and reporting in accordance with AES and regulatory requirements.

- Provide training and guidance to plant personnel on compliance obligations.

- Collaborate with NERC Compliance Team in tracking regulatory changes and assessing their impact on AES Indiana’s generation fleet.

- Collect and submit Quarterly NERC GADS data to MISO.

- Coordinate Annual MISO Generator Capacity Testing and timely submission of test data.

- Provide Operations Electrical Engineering support as needed.

Applicable NERC Reliability Standards  (Power Generation Focus)

- PRC  – Protection and Control (ie.PRC-005, PRC-019, PRC-024)

- FAC  – Facility Design, Connections, and Maintenance (ie.FAC-001, FAC-002)

- MOD  – Modeling, Data, and Analysis (ie.MOD-025, MOD-026, MOD-027)

- VAR  – Voltage and Reactive Control (ie.VAR-002)

- GOP  – Generator Operators (ie. COM-001)

- IRO  – Interconnection Reliability Operations (ie. TOP-001 and IRO-001)

- CIP  – Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP-002 through CIP-013, as applicable to generation assets)

- BAL  – Resource and Demand Balancing (ie. BAL-001, BAL-003)

- EOP  – Emergency Preparedness and Operations (ie. EOP-004, EOP-005, EOP-012)

What We’re Looking For

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. A master’s degree is a plus.

- Experience: Experience in power generation, transmission, NERC compliance, or a related technical environment.

- Strong knowledge of  NERC O&P (Operations & Planning)  and  CIP (Critical Infrastructure Protection)  standards.

- Familiarity with generator protection systems, control systems, and performance modeling.

- Excellent analytical, documentation, and communication skills.

- Ability to manage priorities, collaborate across teams, and follow work through to completion in a dynamic environment.

Preferred Qualifications

- NERC Compliance Certification with Generation Focus on renewable and thermal assets.

- Experience with compliance management software tools.

- Prior participation in NERC audits or investigations.

- Demonstrated ownership, follow-through, and sound judgment when managing work with appropriate guidance and support.

- Strong interpersonal and organizational skills.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Interest in supporting a strong culture of compliance, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Why AES Indiana?
At AES Indiana, you’ll be part of a mission-driven team working to deliver safe, reliable, and sustainable energy. AES offers a collaborative culture where people are encouraged to learn, contribute ideas, and grow their careers while helping shape the future of energy.
We support our people through comprehensive health and well-being benefits, competitive compensation, best-in-class safety and security standards, paid volunteering opportunities, and programs designed to support career development, learning, and professional growth.

The Transmission Planning Operations Engineer will   be responsible for   independently conducting operational planning coordination in connection with the transmission project portfolio, including construction schedule coordination, management of change support, and outage and network model coordination across MISO and PJM.

Job Responsibilities

- Perform with assistance the maintenance of a coordinated construction project list and integrated project schedule, using P6 as the source of schedule data, to provide a common reference across planning, development, engineering, execution, and close-out stages, and to capture project shifts and scope adjustments as they occur.

- Perform with   assistance   quality control review of consultant-prepared construction schedules, including but not limited to Facility Study schedules.

- Perform with   assistance   the annual review of the coordinated project list to inform prioritization and   scope   fidelity as electric network conditions and needs evolve, supporting long-lead material planning and labor resource planning.

- Perform with assistance the team's existing NERC Management of Change compliance structure by evaluating when project changes require review or re-evaluation by the appropriate subject matter experts, including but not limited to PRC-004, PRC-025, PRC-027, FAC-002, and FAC-008, and routing changes to the appropriate owners within the compliance structure.

- Independently support long-term (three-year and one-year) and short-term (three-month) operational planning horizons for outage coordination,   utilizing   power flow models to coordinate planned outages and reduce the risk of projects   failing to obtain   required outage approvals.

- Coordinate outage-related planning input with the System Operations and PMO functions to support holistic outage scheduling across the business.

- Independently manage the MISO and PJM operational/network models and coordinate with the System Planning team on forecasted modeling changes.

- Independently   submit   and maintain tickets in MISO CROW and PJM   eDART   to reflect project and outage-related model changes.

- Provide the Transmission Operations Control   Center   assistance   in times of emergency such as extreme weather events, emergency repairs, or system restoration to ensure   a timely   return to energization of AES customers.

Position Requirements:

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or similar.

- A minimum of 2 years' experience working in the Electric Utility industry

- Ability to perform analysis and prepare engineering deliverables without supervision

- Passing Grade on Fundamentals of Engineering

Highly Desired Skills:

- Bachelor's degree,   certificate   or equivalent experience in power systems studies

- Proficiency   in project scheduling and schedule management, including Primavera P6 or similar software

- Detailed understanding of regulatory frameworks (NERC, FERC, PJM/MISO).

- The ability to communicate complex ideas verbally and in writing.

- Proven technical knowledge and understanding of Transmission grid

- Experience with MISO CROW and/or PJM   eDART   ticket submission and management.

- Experience with MISO and/or   PJM   outage coordination processes and operational/network model submission requirements.

- Working knowledge of power flow modeling concepts and tools (e.g., PSS®E or similar).

The Valuation & Investments (V&I) team is the center of excellence for financial analysis within AES’ U.S. Renewables business. We are seeking a Valuation Associate to support the evaluation of greenfield development and M&A investment opportunities across the U.S., with a focus on solar, wind, and energy storage projects.

In this role, you’ll build complex financial models, collaborate cross-functionally, and contribute directly to key investment decisions that shape our renewable energy pipeline. You’ll work closely with various groups across the organization, gaining exposure to diverse markets and capital structures, while developing deep expertise in renewable project finance.

We're looking for someone who combines technical excellence with strong interpersonal skills, a collaborative mindset, and a passion for clean energy.

Key Responsibilities:

- Support the valuation of renewable energy projects by building and maintaining robust financial models.

- Collaborate with teams across the business, including Development, M&A, Engineering, and Commercial to assess investment opportunities and identify key risks and value drivers.

- Help develop and analyze debt, tax equity, and project equity financing structures.

- Ensure accuracy and consistency of financial metrics presented to senior decision-makers.

- Partner across teams to develop regional strategies, decision-making tools, and analyses that enhance prioritization and innovation.

- Participate in continuous improvement of team tools, templates, and processes.
